entities.summary: Pope John XVII was a short-lived bishop of Rome who briefly occupied the papacy in 1003, marking a period of transition during the late Roman Empire. He was born John Sicco and succeeded Pope John XVI, who was succeeded by Pope John XVIII. Pope John XVII's papacy was marked by power struggles and conflicts with the nobility, particularly the patrician John Crescentius. His legacy is limited to his brief tenure as pope and his role in the complex web of power dynamics within the Roman Catholic Church during this period. The papacy of Pope John XVII was also notable for the fact that he was the last of the popes to be elected under the rule of the Roman Empire, marking the beginning of the end of imperial control over the Church. Pope John XVII's reign was marked by a series of events that would shape the course of Christian history, including the rise of the Holy Roman Empire and the eventual decline of the Roman Empire itself.
